title: Larkspur Community Food Network: regular volunteers drifting away
setting: Larkspur Community Food Network is a fictional regional food-relief nonprofit with four pantry sites (Millbrook, Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane). It relies on about 420 regular volunteers who sort, pack and serve food, including an after-school meals programme for minors at every site. In spring 2026 it introduced a self-scheduling app (RotaWeave) and an annual background-check renewal. After losing a foundation grant, it also eliminated three site coordinator posts. Between March and August the number of active regular volunteers fell sharply, and the board meets on 30 September.
presentingRequest: The executive director wants an independent view of why regular volunteers have stopped coming and what Larkspur should do. She intends to recommend cancelling the RotaWeave contract at the 30 September board meeting unless the evidence points elsewhere.

initialEvidence.source: Mara Ellison, Executive Director, memo to reviewer, 2 September 2026
initialEvidence.text: Our active regular volunteers fell from 421 in March to 295 in August, the worst drop in our eleven years. I have personally taken about a dozen calls from long-serving volunteers who are furious about RotaWeave, the scheduling app we adopted this spring. At the 30 September board meeting I intend to recommend cancelling the RotaWeave contract and going back to the paper rosters that served us for a decade. One board member also thinks Commonplate Volunteers, a new group that opened on 16 June, is poaching our people. I need an independent view of what happened and what we should do before that meeting.

initialEvidence.source: Larkspur project and policy change log (extract)
initialEvidence.text: RotaWeave rollout plan (approved 12 Feb): Millbrook pilot go-live 3 March; Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane go-live 14 April. Basic tier: next week's shifts released to all volunteers every Thursday at 18:00; three staff admin seats; 3-year term, $38,000; early-termination fee $14,000. Policy change (adopted 20 Jan): annual background-check renewal for all regular volunteers, required by the county after-school meals contract and by our insurer for any shift serving minors. Renewal deadline 30 April; volunteers not renewed are deactivated on 1 May until they complete it.

After the loss of the Pellham Foundation operating grant ($171,000), the following savings take effect on 1 May. The site coordinator posts at Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane are eliminated (3.0 FTE, $148,000 annualised), and volunteer oversight at those three sites moves to the regional operations manager. The Millbrook coordinator post is kept because the county senior-meals contract funds it separately. The remaining savings come from reduced van leasing. We recognise this places extra load on site lead volunteers and thank them for their flexibility.

initialEvidence.source: Email from Tobias Wren, Director of Operations and sponsor of the RotaWeave project, to the Executive Director, 28 August 2026
initialEvidence.text: Mara, before the board blames RotaWeave, look at Millbrook. It has been on the app since March, longer than any other site, and its numbers are fine. The slide starts in May, not April. On 1 May we deactivated 23 regulars who hadn't finished their background-check renewal, and plenty more told me the renewal portal was a nightmare. I think the renewal drove people off whether or not they finished it. Cancelling RotaWeave would cost $14k and throw away the attendance data we've finally got for funders. Tobias

Definition: an active regular is a volunteer with 3 or more shifts in the prior 60 days. Org-wide month-end counts: Jan 409, Feb 414, Mar 421, Apr 415, May 384, Jun 345, Jul 315, Aug 295. Renewal deadline: 23 regulars were deactivated on 1 May for an incomplete background-check renewal. Of these, 21 completed it and were reactivated by 31 May; the other 2 have since moved away. Site-level counts are not part of the standard board pack.

initialEvidence.source: Volunteer pulse survey summary, February and June 2026
initialEvidence.text: Anonymous link sent to all regulars. Overall satisfaction (1–5): February mean 4.2 (n=236); June mean 3.5 (n=198). The lowest-scoring item in June was 'ease of getting the shifts I want' at 3.0, down from 4.1. Follow-up: 61 June respondents chose to give their names and were matched to activity records. Of those who scored overall satisfaction at 2 or below, 7 of 19 (37%) were inactive by August, against 4 of 42 (10%) of the rest. Site is not recorded.

catalogue.title: RotaWeave uptime and support-ticket summary, April–August 2026
catalogue.text: Platform uptime was 99.8%, with two incidents (14 May and 9 July) of under 40 minutes each, both outside shift-release windows. There were 46 support tickets: 21 password resets, 11 SMS notification settings, 8 export questions and 6 other. No open defects affect booking. Adoption: 92% of active volunteers at live sites logged in at least once in August. Account manager's note: 'Larkspur is one of our smoothest Basic-tier deployments. We'd welcome a conversation about Plus-tier features.'

catalogue.title: Active regular volunteers by site, monthly, March–August 2026, with each site's go-live and staffing status
catalogue.source: Volunteer database extract, run by the data officer
catalogue.text: Active regular = 3+ shifts in the prior 60 days. Columns run March to August. Millbrook (RotaWeave since 3 Mar; coordinator kept): 118, 117, 116, 114, 112, 111. Dock Street (RotaWeave since 14 Apr; coordinator post ended 1 May): 112, 110, 96, 78, 64, 55. Westgate (RotaWeave since 14 Apr; coordinator post ended 1 May): 105, 103, 88, 70, 58, 49. Quarry Lane (coordinator post ended 1 May; RotaWeave not live because the kiosk tablets were never delivered, go-live moved to 6 Oct; the lead volunteer keeps the paper standing roster): 86, 85, 84, 83, 81, 80. The background-check deadline applied in the same way at all four sites.

catalogue.title: Exit-survey responses from volunteers flagged inactive, May–August 2026
catalogue.source: Automated exit email, responses coded by a volunteer-services intern
catalogue.text: Sent to 141 volunteers flagged inactive; 13 responded (9%). Reasons, coded from free text: busy/other commitments 4, health 2, moved away 1, 'changes at the pantry' 3, prefer not to say 3. The site field was optional and left blank in 11 responses. Sample comments: 'Just a lot going on this summer.' 'Things changed and it didn't feel the same.' 'Might come back in the autumn.'

catalogue.title: Background-check provider processing report, January–May 2026
catalogue.text: Renewal checks submitted: 402. Median turnaround was 3.5 working days, and the 90th percentile was 8 days. 31 applicants were asked to re-upload ID because the image was blurred. Portal availability was 99.5%. The cost is $18 per check, invoiced monthly. Provider's note: 'Submissions peaked in the last ten days before your 30 April deadline, which lengthened median turnaround to 6 days for that fortnight.'

catalogue.title: Volunteer demographics by site, April 2026 snapshot
catalogue.text: Figures are for regular volunteers in April 2026, listed as Millbrook, Dock Street, Westgate, Quarry Lane. Median age: 63, 62, 64, 61. Share aged 70+: 24%, 22%, 26%, 21%. Median tenure: 4.4, 4.1, 4.6, 3.8 years. Share with a smartphone number on file: 81%, 83%, 79%, 80%. Share referred by a corporate partner: 6%, 9%, 7%, 5%.

catalogue.title: Interview with the regional operations manager, 3 September 2026
catalogue.source: Imran Castell, Regional Operations Manager (covering Dock Street, Westgate and Quarry Lane since 1 May)
catalogue.text: 'I can't be at three sites, so I manage from the RotaWeave dashboard. At Dock Street and Westgate the fill rate is above 95% every week, because corporate groups and new sign-ups snap the shifts up, so coverage isn't the problem. Honestly, I think some of the older regulars just didn't want to deal with change, and the renewal paperwork came at the worst possible time. The lead volunteers at each site handle anything day-to-day, and they haven't raised anything urgent with me.'

catalogue.title: Volunteer services booking reconciliation for Dock Street, Westgate and Millbrook, April–August 2026
catalogue.source: Lucia Brandt, Volunteer Services Manager, compiled from RotaWeave audit logs and callback notes
catalogue.text: Basic tier has no recurring bookings, so a regular keeps a weekly slot only if staff book it before Thursday's public release. 'Book on behalf' entries: Millbrook 78–84/week throughout; Dock Street plus Westgate 74/week (14–30 Apr) and 3/week since 1 May. One admin seat has been unused since 1 May. Of 213 April regulars at Dock Street/Westgate, 129 lost their usual slot at least twice in May–June, mostly to new or corporate sign-ups; 114 of them (88%) are now inactive, against 9 of 84 (11%) who kept their slot. At Millbrook, 7 of 117 lost their slot. 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current background check at their last shift. Callbacks reached 61: 44 'lost my regular shift / nobody booked me', 7 health/moving, 5 other commitments, 3 no reason, 2 joined another group.

catalogue.title: Board minutes, 12 February 2026 (RotaWeave procurement)
catalogue.text: Item 4: the Director of Operations presented the RotaWeave proposal, comparing three vendors. The board chose the Basic tier on cost ($38,000 over three years, against $61,000 for Plus). Benefits cited: real-time attendance data for funders, fewer no-shows through SMS reminders, and less coordinator time spent rostering by phone. The treasurer asked about the early-termination terms ($14,000). Motion carried 7–1. Item 5: the board noted the background-check renewal policy adopted on 20 January.

catalogue.title: Commonplate Volunteers public announcements and recruitment posts, June–August 2026
catalogue.source: Public website and social media posts
catalogue.text: Press release, 16 June: Commonplate Volunteers opens a community kitchen on Harlow Street, 0.6 miles from Larkspur's Millbrook site. Its recruitment posts claim '180 volunteers signed up in our first eight weeks'. Roles listed are cooking, delivery driving and front-of-house, on evening and weekend shifts. The posts give no information on where these volunteers previously served.

catalogue.title: Regional food-bank network volunteer benchmarking, 2025–26
catalogue.text: Eleven member organisations took part. Median 6-month retention of regular volunteers was 84% in 2025 and 81% in 2026, with a 2026 range of 72% to 90%. Seven of the 11 respondents cited 'post-pandemic fatigue' or 'cost of living' as pressures. Larkspur did not submit 2026 data. Method: figures are self-reported, and members define 'regular' in different ways.

catalogue.title: Pulse survey item-level results, February and June 2026
catalogue.source: Volunteer pulse survey, full item report
catalogue.text: Item means (1–5), February to June: ease of getting the shifts I want 4.1 → 3.0; I feel valued 4.4 → 3.9; communication from staff 4.0 → 3.4; training adequacy 3.9 → 3.8; would recommend volunteering here 4.5 → 3.9. Coded themes in June free text: 'app' 41 mentions, 'great team' 35, 'staff not around' 22, 'renewal process' 18. The site field was not collected.

catalogue.title: Site coordinator job description and 1 May handover checklist
catalogue.text: Job description (2023): 'Recruit, schedule, support and recognise volunteers; maintain site safety and food-handling logs; liaise with partner agencies.' Handover checklist, Dock Street, signed 30 April: keys and alarm codes to the lead volunteer; food-safety logbooks to the lead volunteer; RotaWeave admin login to the regional operations manager; partner agency contacts to the regional operations manager; volunteer birthday and recognition list to the lead volunteer.

catalogue.title: Monthly food distributed, client visits and volunteer hours, January–August 2026
catalogue.text: Org-wide food distributed (thousand lb): Jan 212, Feb 205, Mar 219, Apr 224, May 221, Jun 230, Jul 236, Aug 229. Client household visits ranged from 9,800 to 10,600 a month with no trend. Recorded volunteer hours were 6,140 in March and 5,520 in August. Corporate-group volunteer hours rose from 410 in March to 1,180 in August.

catalogue.title: County after-school meals contract and insurer safeguarding clauses, January 2026
catalogue.text: County contract §7.3: 'All persons working shifts at which meals are served to minors must hold a background check completed within the previous 12 months. Non-compliance is grounds for suspension of the contract.' Insurer endorsement to Larkspur's general liability policy: cover for abuse or molestation claims depends on annual screening of every volunteer in contact with minors. After-school meals run at all four sites, Monday to Thursday.

catalogue.title: Social-media mentions of Larkspur, April–August 2026
catalogue.text: The monitoring tool captured 37 public mentions. 19 were positive (mostly donation drives and a corporate volunteer day), 11 neutral and 7 negative: three about the scheduling app, two about parking at Westgate and two about client wait times. There was no spike in mention volume, and no posts from accounts identifiable as Larkspur volunteers announcing that they were leaving.

hypotheses.text: The move to app-based self-scheduling, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
The elimination of site coordinator posts, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
The fall in active regular volunteers arose from the move to app-based self-scheduling and the elimination of site coordinator posts acting together; neither change on its own produces it.
The background-check renewal requirement, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.
Recruitment by the newly opened Commonplate Volunteers, on its own, caused the fall in active regular volunteers.

edges.from: Site coordinator post eliminated at a site using app-based self-scheduling
edges.to: Regular volunteers losing their usual weekly shift

edges.from: Regular volunteers losing their usual weekly shift
Background-check renewal requirement with a 30 April deadline
edges.to: Fall in active regular volunteers from May onward

edges.from: Low volunteer satisfaction score in the June pulse survey

actions.text: At Dock Street and Westgate, give a staff member or trained lead volunteer a RotaWeave admin seat and the job of booking regulars into their usual weekly slots before each Thursday release. Phone lapsed regulars to offer them their former slot back, and review re-engagement after 60 days.
Make a volunteer recognition and appreciation programme the centrepiece of the retention response, on the premise that low satisfaction is what is driving regulars to leave.
Suspend the background-check renewal requirement until volunteer numbers recover.
Cancel the RotaWeave contract at all four sites, paying the $14,000 early-termination fee, and return to paper rosters.
Before the board meeting, remove regulars with no shift in the past 45 days from the volunteer roster and from the retention figures.
